scope: Operation GALVANIC pre-tactical mobilization, departure, intelligence signature, readiness/fatigue carry-forward and all-carrier-class visibility before the 1943-11-23 tactical checkpoint.

window.start_band: 1943-11-08..1943-11-10 for slow/assault echelons and initial large-operation signature; fast/CVE carrier departures and rendezvous are staggered through roughly 1943-11-10..16
window.old_branch_D_day: 1943-11-24 planning/comparison datum only; reopened if the reconstructed prelude changes the operation qualitatively
window.rule: Do not materialize fleets at 11/23. Transit, AO rendezvous, CAP/ASW, search, training, maintenance, alert and crew fatigue accrued during this window are paid.

evidence_classes.HARD_BRANCH: Current Branch-B checkpoint/ledger or settled pre-reopen fact.
evidence_classes.HISTORICAL_FALLBACK: Historical date/formation used only where Branch-B has no contrary causal chain.
evidence_classes.CENTERED_REAUDIT: Most-likely working line derived from Branch facts; can move when individual-hull or local-unit trace closes.
evidence_classes.UNRESOLVED: Must be closed before the affected combat event.

qualitative_deltas_already_found.result: Do not inherit the historical torpedo hit. Historical HALIBUT interception was Ultra-cued; Branch B explicitly denies US historical high-grade short-strategic Japanese traffic reconstruction. Centered Junyo reaches the pre-GALVANIC reserve undamaged by that event; uncued submarine encounter remains sensitivity.
qualitative_deltas_already_found.effect: One secondary/medium carrier hull and its deck cycle are materially more available than a naive historical carry-forward would imply.

qualitative_deltas_already_found.item: Marshall air stripping for Operation RO
qualitative_deltas_already_found.result: Do not inherit the historical 12 Nov stripping of 27 Marshall aircraft for Operation RO as an automatic event. Branch South-Pacific geography/campaign chain is different and the historical Rabaul emergency is not a current Branch-B realized dependency.
qualitative_deltas_already_found.effect: Marshall/Gilbert air defense and night-attack wallet is materially larger than historical Galvanic unless a separate Branch transfer ledger proves an equivalent draw.

qualitative_deltas_already_found.item: Bunker Hill pre-GALVANIC wear and staging
qualitative_deltas_already_found.result: Do not copy historical Espiritu Santo/Rabaul sequence because Espiritu Santo is Japanese-held in Branch B. Bunker Hill remains date-valid, but stages through surviving US nodes; she avoids historical Rabaul combat wear while paying different transit/rendezvous costs.
qualitative_deltas_already_found.effect: Lower acute combat fatigue but different logistics/timing; not a free readiness bonus.

qualitative_deltas_already_found.result: Bengal hull commitment centered 0. Secondary carriers remain a two-ocean mobile reserve, then shift Pacific-priority as the US amphibious operation becomes apparent.
qualitative_deltas_already_found.effect: No Bengal-campaign fatigue/deck attrition is charged; routine ferry/patrol/training and subsequent Pacific transit are charged.

fast_carrier_pool_11_23.ready_aircraft_working_band: about 540-590 across the ten fast decks before event-specific CAP/search/recovery reservations; exact squadron roster remains to close
fast_carrier_pool_11_23.fatigue_11_23: LOW_TO_MODERATE overall. September Midway and October Wake experience is paid; roughly a month of replenishment/training reduces acute fatigue. Bunker Hill has less branch combat wear than historical but also less immediate Rabaul combat seasoning.
fast_carrier_pool_11_23.rule: CVL output is not interchangeable with Essex-class output. Preserve deck-cycle, range, recovery, CAP/search burden and mission class.

escort_carrier_pool.working_ready_aircraft_band: about 185-215 total across the eight CVEs; exact VC squadron readiness is separate from fast-carrier strike power
escort_carrier_pool.fatigue_11_23: MODERATE workup/transit burden; generally less fleet-carrier experience and narrower deck margin than TF fast decks.
escort_carrier_pool.rule: Do not treat Liscome Bay as an isolated scripted target. The eight-CVE system is a separate assault-air wallet.

routing_and_departure.historical_anchor: Several Galvanic carrier/CVE elements departed Pearl Harbor on 10 Nov; southern fast-carrier elements historically used Espiritu Santo and sortied around 15 Nov.
routing_and_departure.branch_change: Espiritu Santo and New Caledonia are unavailable to the US. Use Hawaii/Johnston/Canton/Samoa/Funafuti/Efate and at-sea AO rendezvous as event-valid nodes; exact TG routing remains distributed to reduce Midway observability.
routing_and_departure.operational_effect: Small-to-moderate extra scheduling/escort/AO burden, not enough by itself to cancel GALVANIC. It increases pre-departure signature management and makes one synchronized historical departure date inappropriate.

first_line_carriers.ready_aircraft_working_band: about 270-290 across the four decks before mission-specific reservations
first_line_carriers.fatigue_11_23: LOW. The core has been conserved as fleet-in-being; alert/search/training activity rises in mid-November but no Bengal charge is applied.
first_line_carriers.employment: Do not auto-sortie to save Tarawa/Makin. Positive-EV contact freshness, US mission-state separation, fuel/escort and recovery geometry remain gates.

Junyo.hull: CENTERED AVAILABLE; historical 11/05 HALIBUT damage not inherited
Junyo.role: low-speed medium carrier; rear/mobile reserve, ferry/CAP/search/limited strike, can free first-line deck burden
Junyo.fatigue: LOW_TO_MODERATE depending on final eastward transit timing

Hiyo.hull: CENTERED AVAILABLE after prior repair/workup; no Bengal combat charge
Hiyo.role: low-speed medium carrier; reserve/ferry/CAP/limited strike rather than first-line fast strike equivalence

Ryujo.hull: CENTERED AVAILABLE; released from Aleutians after May intervention
Ryujo.role: forward light deck for search/CAP/ferry/limited strike under suitable wind/load
Ryujo.fatigue: LOW_TO_MODERATE; routine duty only before alert

Zuiho.role: forward light deck for CAP/search/ferry/limited strike and deck-load sharing

secondary_carriers_mandatory_trace.combined_ready_aircraft_working_band: about 105-130 across Junyo/Hiyo/Ryujo/Zuiho if all are individually released for Pacific use; do not assume all four are in one task group or inside immediate strike radius on 11/23
secondary_carriers_mandatory_trace.posture: two-ocean strategic reserve until RN eastern return fails to materialize; Pacific-priority once US amphibious threat is recognized; routine ferry/patrol/training followed by maintenance/rest.

secondary_carriers_background_trace.rule: Both are kept visible as date-valid/survival-path candidates, but contribute zero to the immediate combat wallet until individual location, air group and deck readiness are closed. Re-open in depth for the later Eastern Fleet return audit.

marshall_gilbert_air_and_water_air.historical_operation_RO_guard: Historical Galvanic had 27 aircraft stripped from the Marshalls on 12 Nov for Operation RO, leaving only 46; do not import that drain without a Branch-equivalent transfer event.

legacy_candidate_revalidated_structure.land_fighters_capable_of_Gilberts_reacti: roughly 80-95 physical-class across the Marshall network before suppression, with ready count lower/event-specific
legacy_candidate_revalidated_structure.attack_aircraft_land_or_carrier_type: roughly 35-45 physical-class available across the network; night-qualified fraction is smaller
legacy_candidate_revalidated_structure.legacy_recon_flying_boat_floatplane_core: roughly 15-20 physical-class before adding the new small Zuiun layer
legacy_candidate_revalidated_structure.Kyofu: roughly 12-20 physical / 8-16 normally ready across priority Gilbert-Marshall lagoon nodes as a working allocation, not at every island
legacy_candidate_revalidated_structure.Zuiun: roughly 5-9 physical / 4-7 ready across Marshall-side nodes by 11/23 as a working first-detachment allocation; high-utilization search/contact asset, not an independent strike unit

marshall_gilbert_air_and_water_air.fatigue_11_23: MODERATE in search/recon and selected alert units because activity rises during the US mobilization window; less operational depletion than historical Operation-RO-stripped force.
marshall_gilbert_air_and_water_air.mission_system_rule: Use broad search -> suspicious contact -> re-search -> fast confirmation -> track/handoff. Zuiun and D4Y improve contact freshness; Kyofu preserves a local air layer after runway suppression. Neither is a flat air-strength multiplier.

night_surface_confidence.effect: Selected trained cruiser/DD groups may be more willing and better prepared to attempt a one-pass Long-Lance ambush after passive ESM warning/bearing history.
night_surface_confidence.limit: This does not create confidence in a prolonged SG/CIC radar gun duel. US may still obtain the first weapon-quality track.

mobilization_intelligence_sequence.US: Slow/assault echelons, oilers, escorts and carrier groups begin leaving/assembling in distributed fashion. Southern doglegs and at-sea rendezvous pay extra branch logistics cost.
mobilization_intelligence_sequence.Japan: Traffic/DF/recon/submarine observation and missing-US-shipping indicators raise probability of a major operation, but target class remains broad. No high-grade US/Japanese magic decrypt is allowed.

mobilization_intelligence_sequence.US: Fast and escort carrier concentration becomes difficult to hide as an operation-scale signature; CAP/ASW/drills and refueling begin accumulating transit fatigue.
mobilization_intelligence_sequence.Japan: Amphibious character becomes more likely than a pure carrier raid. Secondary carriers terminate nonessential routine tasks, perform maintenance/rest, and Pacific-priority movement begins where location permits. First-line core goes to higher readiness without automatic sortie.

mobilization_intelligence_sequence.US: Pre-assault suppression/recon geometry and fleet tracks increasingly point toward the Gilbert-Marshall axis, although exact landing objective need not be known instantly.
mobilization_intelligence_sequence.Japan: Marshalls/Gilberts raise search/CAP/dispersion and submarine/light-surface readiness. The absence of a historical Operation-RO drain makes this alert more consequential and also raises Japanese pre-contact fuel/engine-hour/fatigue expenditure.

mobilization_intelligence_sequence.US: Assault force and carrier cover approach tactical operating areas; fast-deck strike power is split among suppression, fleet defense, search and support rather than one homogeneous carrier mass.
mobilization_intelligence_sequence.Japan: Target inference tightens. Forward water aviation, submarines and light night forces enter the contact chain; carrier main body remains gated by contact freshness and US mission-state separation. 11/23 checkpoint is reached with paid alert fatigue rather than a fresh materialization.

first_contact_boundary.next: Resolve first Japanese external contact and the first light/night surface opportunity using the contact-quality ladder and the above paid prelude.
must_close_before_weapon_release: exact local Marshall/Gilbert ready aircraft by base and type
